To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
transfusions are associated with increased adverse outcomes in cardiac surgical patients irrespective of the patient's nadir hematocrit.
the effect of transfusions on postoperative outcomes was greater than that of anemia in patients undergoing on-pumping cardiac surgery.
transfusions are associated with worse post-operative cardiac surgery patient outcomes, regardless of the nadir HCT.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of anemia and transfusions on post-operative outcomes following cardiac surgical procedures.
the role of transfusion and anemia on peri-operative outcomes.
the impact of intra-operative transfusions and anemia on post-operative outcomes in patients undergoing cardiac surgery.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
transfusions have an impact on adverse outcomes irrespective nadir HCT, and that the impact is more pronounced in the setting of higher nadir HCT.
transfusions have more of a negative impact on patient outcomes than anemia in the peri-operative setting.
the relationship between intra-operative nadir hematocrit and the transfusion of red blood cell units on post-operative outcomes after cardiac surgery is complex and multifactorial.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
transfusions should be avoided in patients undergoing cardiac surgery.
anemia is not a significant predictor for post-operative outcomes after cardiac surgery.
the optimal strategy for management of anemia is to maintain a nadir HCT > 21.
The main takeaway from our work is that
transfusions have an adverse impact on outcomes, regardless of an individual’s nadir hematocrit.
transfusions should be avoided whenever possible.
the impact of anemia on post-operative outcomes is not as significant as the impact of transfusions.
